thread:
sam: quick note — host-side CPU tail on streaming path during the last traffic spike. saw node at ~35% cpu for parse stage even though GPU & runtime idle.
mira: ugh. any flame graph / perf report? rough window?
sam: attached quick snapshot (pprof): parse_allocs -> normalize_utf8 -> proto_unmarshal heavy. happens when chunked frames ~6-12KB and when clients send many small messages in one stream.
alex: can you paste the allocation sample? guessing we're doing a few copies per chunk: readbuf -> decode -> normalize -> proto copy
sam: yeah, snippet:
```
# pprof top
27.3%  parse_allocs
18.1%  normalize_utf8
12.4%  proto.Unmarshal
 9.8%  bytes.Repeat / slice growth
```
Also observed 3x more GC cycles during spikes.
dana: is this the same flow as the recent streaming-slab changes? we changed preparse buffer sizing last week.
sam: similar time window. I rolled a canary that reintroduced the old preparse fence and the spike went down ~40% in cpu tail.
mira: interesting. hypothesis: the new preparse tried to avoid copies but increased intermediate allocations when frames cross boundary. maybe reallocation churn.
alex: two quick ideas:
- rework the preparse to try in-place utf8 validate (avoid normalize unless invalid)
- keep a pooled buffer per connection to avoid slice growth on frame boundaries
sam: experimented with buffer pool + in-place check. result: median parse cpu -22%, p50 end-to-end latency unchanged, p99 improved slightly. memory stable.
dana: any impact on kvcache or batching? could reduce latency variability which helps batching heuristics.
sam: no negative impact observed. actually KV cache hit-rate steady; slight reduction in requeues.
infra-bot: deploy triggered: slim-proto-parse-pool @staging by sam
mira: can we add a microbenchmark that simulates crossing-frame UTF-8 and protobuf partial reads? we should catch regressions in CI.
alex: will add a small harness in eng-runtime/perf with parameters: chunk_size, boundary_offset, concurrency
sam: also noted grpc HTTP/2 WINDOW_UPDATE interactions — when we hold pooled buffer too long, we block window and client stalls. need careful buffer lifetime.
dana: maybe move to ephemeral borrow semantics: pool but hand off ownership on first WINDOW_UPDATE or end-of-frame.
mira: good call. for now let's ship pool + in-place UTF8 check to canary and watch CPU/GC. add perf test ASAP.
sam: filing follow-up: https://redwood-internal/issue/RT-2481 (putting numbers and perf graphs there). will update thread.
alex: thanks — triage looks actionable. me and mira will pair on harness tomorrow. :thumbsup:
sam: thanks all. tracking in RT-2481.
